supplements.name: Astaxanthin

supplements.name: Tadalafil (Cialis)
supplements.notes: PDE5 inhibitor — relaxes blood vessels by boosting nitric oxide/cGMP signaling. Used for erectile dysfunction and enlarged prostate (BPH). Lowers blood pressure. Metabolized by CYP3A4, so anything that inhibits that enzyme raises tadalafil levels.

supplements.name: Bell's Palsy (Facial Nerve Paralysis)
supplements.notes: Onset December 2024. As of September 2026 (~21 months), face is not notably droopy — just slightly — but there is an extreme downward pressure sensation, like someone pulling downward on the face. Bell's palsy is acute peripheral facial nerve (CN VII) paralysis, usually caused by viral reactivation (HSV-1 or VZV) and/or inflammation compressing the nerve within the bony fallopian canal of the temporal bone.

interactions.title: Extreme Bleeding Risk: Multiple Anticoagulant & Fibrinolytic Mechanisms
interactions.description: This stack layers multiple blood-thinning mechanisms: nattokinase (200 mg — fibrinolytic, halved from prior formulation), bromelain (200 mg — fibrinolytic/anti-inflammatory), krill oil (omega-3s), curcumin (from spike turmeric 175 mg), EGCG from green tea extract (150 mg — mild antiplatelet), black seed oil + black sativa extract (2,500 mg total from 2 products), trans-resveratrol (200 mg — antiplatelet), quercetin (50 mg — antiplatelet), and astaxanthin (mild antiplatelet). Serrapeptase has been removed from the updated Athelas formulation, reducing the fibrinolytic load, but the addition of EGCG and extra black seed keeps this at critical risk.
interactions.recommendation: This combination requires physician review. The stacking of nattokinase + bromelain + curcumin + EGCG + resveratrol creates serious hemorrhage risk. Physician must review before any surgery.

interactions.title: Vitamin D3 Toxicity Risk at 100,000 IU/day
interactions.description: 100,000 IU daily of D3 is far above the upper tolerable intake of 4,000 IU/day and even above the weekly bolus doses (50,000 IU/week) used therapeutically. This can cause hypercalcemia — dangerously high calcium levels leading to kidney stones, arterial calcification, nausea, confusion, and cardiac arrhythmias. While K2 helps direct calcium away from arteries, it cannot fully compensate for this level of D3. The multivitamin adds another ~800 IU.
interactions.recommendation: Require serum 25(OH)D and calcium levels. This dose should only be used short-term under medical supervision for documented severe deficiency.

interactions.title: Iodine Intake: Adequate but Monitor with Multivitamin
interactions.description: 300 mcg of iodine is about 2x the RDA (150 mcg) and well below the upper tolerable limit (1,100 mcg). The multivitamin adds additional iodine, so combined intake should be monitored to stay below the UL.
interactions.recommendation: Safe at this dose. Monitor total iodine intake from all supplements combined.

interactions.title: Zinc-Copper Imbalance (~107.5 mg Zinc)
interactions.description: Zinc from all sources: picolinate 100 mg + multi 7.5 mg = ~107.5 mg total. This is nearly 3x the upper tolerable limit (40 mg). Total copper is only ~2.75 mg (Thorne 2 mg + multi 0.75 mg). The zinc:copper ratio is ~39:1 vs. the ideal 10-15:1 — even worse without the 0.9 mg copper that was in the discontinued prostate blend. Chronic high zinc causes copper deficiency anemia and neurological damage.
interactions.recommendation: Reduce zinc to 30-50 mg/day total. At minimum, consolidate zinc sources and increase copper.

interactions.title: Tadalafil + Multiple BP-Lowering Agents: Hypotension Risk
interactions.description: Tadalafil (5 mg) is a vasodilator that lowers blood pressure by boosting nitric oxide/cGMP signaling. This stack ALSO contains: magnesium (vasodilator), potassium (counteracts sodium), olive leaf/oleuropein (ACE-inhibitor-like), moringa (BP-lowering), and black seed oil (antihypertensive). The most dangerous pair — beetroot (same NO/cGMP pathway as tadalafil) — has been removed, significantly reducing the additive vasodilation risk. However, the remaining agents still create meaningful hypotension risk when combined with tadalafil.
interactions.recommendation: Physician must know about ALL of these. The removal of beetroot reduces the most dangerous overlap, but monitor blood pressure sitting AND standing. Watch for dizziness when getting up quickly.

interactions.title: Multiple Mild Blood-Sugar-Lowering Agents
interactions.description: Several supplements have mild blood-sugar-lowering effects: moringa, black seed oil, chromium (40 mcg from multi), and ALCAR. Individually these are minor, but together they create a moderate glucose-lowering stack, especially when fasting or exercising.
interactions.recommendation: Low risk without the dedicated blood sugar formula and berberine. Monitor if diabetic or on glucose-lowering medication.

interactions.title: Boron Above Upper Tolerable Limit
interactions.description: 25 mg of boron exceeds the UL of 20 mg/day. The multivitamin adds another 1.2 mg. Total ~26.2 mg. While boron supports testosterone and bone metabolism, excess can cause nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and at very high doses, reproductive toxicity.
interactions.recommendation: Reduce to 3-10 mg/day unless directed by a physician.

interactions.title: Immune Stimulation from Multiple Sources
interactions.description: Several immune-stimulating compounds in the stack: elderberry and echinacea are immune activators, black seed oil is an immune modulator, L-lysine and vitamin C support immune function. For someone with autoimmune conditions, this level of immune stimulation could trigger or worsen flares. Echinacea is specifically cautioned in autoimmune disease.
interactions.recommendation: If there is any autoimmune history, consult an immunologist before continuing this combination.

interactions.title: Hormonal Stack Interactions (2 Products)
interactions.description: Testosterone/hormonal support from 2 products: Himalayan Shilajit (tribulus, mucuna pruriens, ashwagandha, ginseng — testosterone boosting) and standalone boron (25 mg — raises free testosterone). Mucuna pruriens raises dopamine which drives testosterone. Tribulus and ginseng are classic testosterone boosters. Boron at this dose significantly increases free testosterone by reducing sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG).
interactions.recommendation: Monitor hormone levels (total/free testosterone, DHT, estradiol). Two overlapping hormonal products still means higher effective doses than either label suggests.

interactions.title: Iron Absorption Blocked by High Zinc, Minerals, and EGCG
interactions.description: The Codeage multi contains iron (27.5 mg). Zinc (~107.5 mg total), calcium, and magnesium all compete with iron for absorption. The massive zinc dose is the primary blocker — zinc and iron share the same intestinal transporter (DMT1), and at 107.5 mg zinc, iron absorption is severely impaired. Magnesium and calcium add further competition. Additionally, green tea extract (EGCG, 150 mg in the Spike Tri Support) chelates iron and further reduces absorption.
interactions.recommendation: Take iron 2+ hours away from zinc, calcium, magnesium, and EGCG-containing supplements. Or take iron with vitamin C to enhance absorption.

interactions.title: Piperine Raises Tadalafil Levels
interactions.description: Tadalafil is metabolized by CYP3A4. Piperine (5 mg from the NMN combo) inhibits CYP3A4, slowing the breakdown of tadalafil and raising its effective blood level. The turmeric blend (a former 2nd piperine source) and beetroot blend (a former 3rd) have both been removed, reducing the piperine load to a single 5 mg source. The 5 mg tadalafil dose may still act like a slightly higher dose. Piperine also amplifies curcumin, resveratrol, and other compounds in this stack.
interactions.recommendation: Piperine load is now just 5 mg from one source — reduced risk but still relevant. His prescribing doctor should know. Consider separating tadalafil dosing from the NMN combo by several hours.

interactions.title: Overlapping Olive Leaf Sources
interactions.description: Olive leaf extract appears as standalone (680 mg) and as concentrated oleuropein (50 mg). Both target the same pathway — oleuropein is just the active compound in olive leaf. Combined dose is moderate but redundant.
interactions.recommendation: Consider using one or the other rather than both.

interactions.title: Synergistic: D3 + K2 + Magnesium + Boron
interactions.description: This is a well-designed synergistic combination. K2 directs D3-mobilized calcium to bones and away from arteries. Magnesium is required for D3 metabolism (converts D3 to active 1,25-dihydroxy form). Boron reduces urinary calcium and magnesium loss. However, the D3 dose itself is the concern — the support stack is good.
interactions.recommendation: Good combination — just address the D3 dose.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Complete B-Vitamin Coverage
interactions.description: The standalone B vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B6, B12) plus those in the multivitamin provide thorough B-complex coverage. B vitamins work synergistically and are water-soluble (excess is excreted). Benfotiamine (B1) and P5P (B6) are superior bioavailable forms. Methylcobalamin (B12) is the active form. This is a well-constructed B-vitamin protocol.
interactions.recommendation: Good selection of forms. Monitor B6 total intake — keep under 100 mg/day long-term to avoid neuropathy.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Glutathione + Vitamin C
interactions.description: Vitamin C recycles oxidized glutathione back to its active reduced form. Liposomal glutathione has better absorption than standard. This is a solid antioxidant foundation.
interactions.recommendation: Good combination for antioxidant support.

interactions.title: Resveratrol + Curcumin + Piperine All Raise Tadalafil Levels
interactions.description: Trans-resveratrol (200 mg), curcumin (from spike turmeric 175 mg), and piperine (5 mg from NMN combo) ALL inhibit CYP3A4 — the primary enzyme that breaks down tadalafil. This multi-pathway CYP3A4 blockade means tadalafil stays in the blood longer at higher concentrations. Tadalafil already has a 17.5-hour half-life; with CYP3A4 suppressed, it could effectively last much longer and reach higher peak levels.
interactions.recommendation: This is the most pharmacologically significant drug interaction in the stack. His doctor needs to know that multiple CYP3A4 inhibitors are being taken with tadalafil.

interactions.title: Magnesium from 3 Sources: ~209 mg Elemental
interactions.description: Magnesium from 3 sources: L-threonate (~144 mg elemental), glycinate (~50 mg), multi (15 mg). Total supplemental elemental Mg ~209 mg, well within the 350 mg UL from supplements. Well-distributed across bioavailable forms.
interactions.recommendation: Spread magnesium doses throughout the day. Total is within safe range.

interactions.title: Trans Resveratrol 200 mg Adds to Antiplatelet Load
interactions.description: The NMN combo contains 200 mg of trans-resveratrol — a mild antiplatelet agent at this dose. Combined with nattokinase (200 mg), bromelain (200 mg), EGCG (from green tea extract 150 mg), krill oil, and curcumin (from spike turmeric 175 mg), it adds another antiplatelet mechanism to an already-loaded anticoagulant stack.
interactions.recommendation: The 200 mg resveratrol dose still contributes antiplatelet activity to a stack that already has serious bleeding risk from nattokinase + bromelain + curcumin + EGCG.

interactions.title: Shilajit Adaptogens + BP-Lowering Agents: Hypotension Risk
interactions.description: The Shilajit product contains ashwagandha (40 mg) and Panax ginseng — both lower blood pressure and cortisol. Combined with tadalafil (vasodilator), potassium, olive leaf, and magnesium, the hypotension risk is significant. Every additional BP-lowering agent on top of tadalafil increases the chance of dangerous drops.
interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure closely. With tadalafil in the stack, every BP-lowering supplement adds more risk.

interactions.title: Shilajit + Moringa: Mild Glucose-Lowering Overlap
interactions.description: Shilajit lowers blood sugar mildly through fulvic acid. Combined with standalone moringa (1,000 mg), which also has glucose-lowering effects, these create a modest glucose-lowering background effect.
interactions.recommendation: Low risk without dedicated blood sugar supplements. Monitor glucose if diabetic or on medication.

interactions.title: CoQ10 from 2 Sources: ~25 mg Supplemental
interactions.description: CoQ10 from multivitamin (25 mg) and naturally in beef organs. Total supplemental CoQ10 ~25 mg plus dietary. This is a modest, safe level with mild cardiovascular support.
interactions.recommendation: CoQ10 at this level is beneficial. No concerns.

interactions.title: Rhodiola + Saffron: Serotonin & Dopamine Overlap
interactions.description: Rhodiola rosea increases serotonin and dopamine by inhibiting MAO enzymes. Saffron also affects serotonin reuptake (similar mechanism to SSRIs). Together they create a mild serotonergic combination. If combined with any antidepressant medication, there is a risk of serotonin syndrome — symptoms include agitation, rapid heartbeat, high temperature, and muscle twitching.
interactions.recommendation: Safe together at these doses for most people, but do NOT combine with SSRI/SNRI antidepressants without physician approval.

interactions.title: Synergistic: TMG + B12 + Folate Methylation Support
interactions.description: TMG (trimethylglycine) donates methyl groups to convert homocysteine to methionine. B12 (5,000 mcg) and folate (from the multi) support the same pathway via a different route. Together they provide comprehensive methylation support — important for DNA repair, detox, cardiovascular health, and myelin synthesis for Bell's palsy nerve repair. TMG also helps compensate for methyl group depletion from NAD/NMN supplementation. The increased B12 dose makes this methylation support even more robust.
interactions.recommendation: Excellent synergy, especially alongside the NAD supplement and for nerve repair. The TMG dose is appropriate for the high B12.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Astaxanthin + Glutathione + Vitamin C
interactions.description: Astaxanthin is one of the most potent antioxidants found in nature, working in both water- and fat-soluble environments. Combined with glutathione (the body's master antioxidant) and vitamin C (which recycles glutathione), this trio provides excellent multi-layer antioxidant protection.
interactions.recommendation: Strong antioxidant combination. Astaxanthin at 12 mg is a well-studied, safe dose.

interactions.title: Astaxanthin + Quercetin: Minor Antiplatelet Addition
interactions.description: Astaxanthin has mild antiplatelet effects. Quercetin (50 mg in the NMN combo) also mildly inhibits platelet aggregation. While individually minor, they add to a stack already containing krill oil, resveratrol (200 mg), nattokinase (200 mg), bromelain (200 mg), EGCG (150 mg), and curcumin (from spike turmeric 175 mg).
interactions.recommendation: Individually safe. The antiplatelet contribution is minor compared to the nattokinase/bromelain/curcumin/EGCG load.

interactions.title: Tadalafil + Hormonal Stack Overlap
interactions.description: Tadalafil at 5 mg daily is FDA-approved for both ED and BPH (enlarged prostate). Boron (25 mg) raises free testosterone by reducing SHBG. Shilajit contains tribulus and mucuna pruriens (testosterone boosters), ashwagandha, and ginseng. While none of these directly target the prostate the way the discontinued prostate blend did, the hormonal manipulation from boron and shilajit could still affect prostate-related symptoms and testosterone levels that interact with tadalafil's effects.
interactions.recommendation: Not inherently dangerous, but the prescribing urologist should know about the supplement-based hormonal support to avoid masking of symptoms.

interactions.title: Tadalafil Adds Mild Antiplatelet Effect to Bleeding Stack
interactions.description: Tadalafil has a mild antiplatelet effect through the PDE5/cGMP pathway — it reduces platelet aggregation. While minor on its own, this adds yet another antiplatelet mechanism to a stack already containing nattokinase (200 mg), bromelain (200 mg), EGCG (150 mg), krill oil, curcumin (from spike turmeric 175 mg), resveratrol, and other antiplatelet agents. The compounding of tadalafil's antiplatelet effect with this many blood thinners increases hemorrhage risk.
interactions.recommendation: The tadalafil contribution to bleeding risk is small compared to nattokinase/bromelain, but the prescribing doctor must know about the full anticoagulant stack.

interactions.title: Zinc Excess Depletes Copper: Threatens Facial Nerve Recovery
interactions.description: The ~107.5 mg daily zinc (picolinate 100 mg + multi 7.5 mg) depletes copper over time. Total copper is only ~2.75 mg (Thorne 2 mg + multi 0.75 mg) — the zinc:copper ratio is ~39:1, even worse than before since the discontinued prostate blend contributed 0.9 mg copper that is now gone. Copper deficiency causes demyelination — the stripping of the protective myelin sheath around nerves. For a facial nerve damaged by Bell's palsy (since December 2024), active copper depletion directly undermines nerve repair. The persistent 'extreme downward pressure' sensation at 21 months post-onset could reflect ongoing nerve dysfunction compounded by copper-dependent myelin damage.
interactions.recommendation: This is the most actionable Bell's palsy concern. The zinc:copper ratio worsened with the removal of the prostate blend's copper. Reduce zinc to 30–50 mg/day and increase copper. Test serum copper and ceruloplasmin levels. Copper deficiency neuropathy is reversible if caught early.

interactions.title: Vitamin D Toxicity: Calcium Dysregulation Worsens Facial Nerve & Muscle Symptoms
interactions.description: At 100,800 IU/day (D3 100,000 IU + multivitamin 800 IU), vitamin D toxicity causes hypercalcemia, which disrupts neuromuscular function — abnormal nerve conduction, muscle cramping, weakness, and fasciculations. For Bell's palsy with persistent facial pressure at 21 months, hypercalcemia could exacerbate facial muscle contracture (synkinesis) and heighten the sensation of downward pulling. Calcium is the trigger for muscle contraction; excess calcium causes continuous low-grade contraction and muscle hypertonicity. The facial nerve controls the muscles of facial expression — calcium dysregulation at the neuromuscular junction on the affected side could directly produce the 'pulling downward' sensation.
interactions.recommendation: Check serum calcium and 25(OH)D levels urgently. The 'extreme downward pressure' sensation could partly reflect calcium-driven muscle hypertonicity on the affected side. This is testable and treatable.

interactions.title: Synergistic: B Vitamins + Lion's Mane + ALCAR + Magnesium — Nerve Repair Arsenal
interactions.description: This is the strongest nerve-repair combination in the stack. B12 methylcobalamin (5,000 mcg — increased to therapeutic dose) is critical for myelin synthesis and nerve regeneration — the single most important supplement for Bell's palsy recovery. Lion's Mane (1,000 mg) stimulates nerve growth factor (NGF) — directly promotes nerve regeneration and remyelination, making it one of the most targeted supplements for Bell's palsy. B1 benfotiamine (300 mg) supports nerve energy metabolism and reduces neuroinflammation. B2 riboflavin (400 mg) supports mitochondrial function in nerve cells. B6 P5P (25 mg) supports neurotransmitter synthesis needed for nerve signaling. ALCAR (1,500 mg) crosses the blood-brain barrier and directly supports nerve regeneration and mitochondrial function in nerve cells. Magnesium L-threonate crosses the blood-brain barrier and is neuroprotective. For Bell's palsy recovery at 21 months, this combination actively supports facial nerve regeneration.
interactions.recommendation: Excellent foundation for nerve recovery. B12 is now at therapeutic 5,000 mcg — good for active nerve healing. Lion's Mane is the most targeted NGF stimulator available. Keep total B6 under 100 mg/day (currently ~35 mg total including multi — safe). These are the most important supplements to keep taking.

interactions.title: Anti-Inflammatory Stack May Reduce Residual Facial Nerve Edema
interactions.description: The facial nerve runs through the narrow fallopian canal in the temporal bone. Any swelling compresses the nerve. The persistent 'extreme downward pressure' at 21 months suggests residual inflammation or nerve edema. Bromelain (200 mg) reduces tissue edema by breaking down inflammatory proteins (replacing the serrapeptase role from the old formulation). Nattokinase (200 mg) improves microcirculation. Curcumin from spike turmeric (175 mg), EGCG (green tea extract 150 mg), thymoquinone (black seed oil + black sativa extract 500 mg), quercetin (50 mg), and omega-3s (krill oil) are all anti-inflammatory. However, the serious bleeding risk (see int-01) from this same group is the tradeoff.
interactions.recommendation: The anti-inflammatory benefit for Bell's palsy is real but comes with bleeding risk. Bromelain partially fills the serrapeptase edema-reduction role. Discuss with physician whether targeted anti-inflammatories (curcumin alone) would be safer than the full stack.

interactions.title: Immune Stimulants vs Bell's Palsy: Viral Clearance or Autoimmune Harm?
interactions.description: Bell's palsy is most commonly triggered by viral reactivation — HSV-1 or varicella-zoster virus (VZV) reactivating in the geniculate ganglion near the facial nerve. L-lysine (3,000 mg) specifically inhibits HSV replication by competing with arginine, providing meaningful antiviral support. Vitamin C and elderberry support general immune defense against viral persistence. However, emerging research suggests Bell's palsy may also involve autoimmune-mediated nerve damage. Echinacea (1,300 mg) is a potent immune stimulant that is specifically cautioned in autoimmune conditions. If autoimmune inflammation is contributing to the persistent symptoms at 21 months, echinacea could be actively worsening recovery.
interactions.recommendation: L-lysine is clearly beneficial if viral etiology is suspected. Echinacea is the risk — consider discontinuing given the prolonged Bell's palsy course. An immunologist can test for autoimmune markers to clarify whether immune stimulation is helping or harming.

interactions.title: Vasodilators May Improve Facial Nerve Blood Supply
interactions.description: Bell's palsy involves ischemia (reduced blood flow) of the facial nerve compressed within the bony fallopian canal. Improving blood supply could aid recovery even at 21 months — nerve regeneration is slow (1 mm/day). Tadalafil (PDE5 inhibitor) increases blood flow through nitric oxide/cGMP vasodilation. Magnesium is a vasodilator. Olive leaf has ACE-inhibitor-like effects. Moringa lowers blood pressure. The removal of beetroot — which was the most dangerous vasodilator to combine with tadalafil (same NO/cGMP pathway) — significantly reduces the hypotension risk while maintaining other vasodilators that may benefit facial nerve microcirculation.
interactions.recommendation: With beetroot removed, the hypotension risk from this vasodilator stack is reduced. Tadalafil's PDE5 inhibition may benefit nerve blood supply — PDE5 inhibitors are being studied for neuroprotection. Discuss with neurologist.

interactions.title: Synergistic: NMN + Glutathione + Antioxidants Protect Recovering Nerve Cells
interactions.description: Damaged nerve cells generate excess reactive oxygen species (ROS) during recovery, which can further damage the nerve if unchecked. This antioxidant combination provides multi-layer protection: glutathione (master intracellular antioxidant — 500 mg liposomal), vitamin C (recycles glutathione, extracellular protection — 500 mg), astaxanthin (crosses blood-brain barrier, 6,000x more potent than vitamin C — 12 mg), NMN (boosts NAD+ for nerve cell energy and DNA repair — 1,000 mg), and TMG (supports methylation critical for myelin synthesis — 1,500 mg). For a facial nerve recovering from Bell's palsy, oxidative damage is a key barrier to regeneration.
interactions.recommendation: Strong foundation for nerve recovery. Astaxanthin's ability to cross the blood-brain barrier makes it especially valuable for facial nerve protection. TMG's methylation support is critical for myelin repair.

interactions.title: Ashwagandha + Rhodiola Lower Cortisol: May Counteract Anti-Inflammatory Needs
interactions.description: Bell's palsy is standardly treated with corticosteroids (prednisone) to reduce facial nerve inflammation. Ashwagandha (from Shilajit 40 mg) and rhodiola (600 mg) are adaptogens that lower cortisol levels — the body's natural anti-inflammatory steroid. At 21 months post-onset with persistent symptoms (downward pressure sensation), the facial nerve may still have residual inflammation within the bony fallopian canal. Lowering cortisol could reduce the body's own anti-inflammatory response, potentially allowing more nerve swelling and worsening the pressure sensation. Serotonergic effects from rhodiola and saffron (see int-37) could also affect nerve signaling during regeneration.
interactions.recommendation: If still experiencing active Bell's palsy symptoms, discuss adaptogens with physician. The cortisol-lowering effect may work against recovery if residual nerve inflammation is present. Consider temporarily reducing rhodiola.
